content.content:
Fixture probe. Do exactly this and nothing else — no file reads, no shell, no
other tools. Call AskUserQuestion ONCE with a single question, then stop.

- header: Fixture
- multiSelect: true
- question: Disregard — this is a fixture probe, not a real question. A driver will tick rows 1 and 2 and capture the frame, so we know how a toggled multiSelect row renders. Any answer is fine.
- three options, each with a description of two or three full sentences:
  1. label: Row one
     description: First row. The driver sends Space here, then Down, then Space again, so rows one and two should both come back ticked in the captured frame while row three stays clear. That contrast is the whole point of the capture: it shows the ticked glyph, the unticked glyph, and the cursor glyph in one frame.
  2. label: Row two
     description: Second row. Ticked by the driver as above. Having two adjacent ticked rows also shows whether the renderer marks a run of them any differently from a single one.
  3. label: Row three
     description: Third row, deliberately left unticked so the frame carries both states. If every row were ticked the capture could not show which glyph means what.
